pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

comment.comment:
$HOOKS — BNB Chain’s new hook meta

I think $HOOKS is one of those coins people can easily overlook at first.

pickhooks is basically a launchpad on BNB Chain where the tokens themselves can have rules built into the contract.

Not just another copy-paste launchpad.

You can choose things like holder limits, slow mode, anti-sniper mechanics, jackpots and other trading rules. Up to 8 rules can be selected, and once the token launches they can’t simply be changed by the dev. (pickhooks)

That’s a pretty interesting concept for memecoins.

The other thing I like is that $HOOKS actually has a reason to exist within the platform.

Every trade on tokens launched through pickhooks generates fees. Part of the platform fee is used to buy back and burn $HOOKS. The project is already showing the amount burned and BNB spent on buybacks on its own site. (pickhooks)

So if the launchpad gets more activity, the token should theoretically benefit from that activity.

And we’re still very early.

The token is currently around the sub-$1M market-cap range, with roughly 1.3k–1.5k holders depending on the tracker. Liquidity is also still relatively small. (ApeSpace)

Obviously this is high risk. It’s a brand-new launchpad and there is no guarantee that pickhooks becomes a major BNB Chain platform.

But I like the setup.

New chain narrative + launchpad + programmable rules + fee-based buybacks/burns + low market cap.

If pickhooks starts getting real volume and launches a few coins that actually run, $HOOKS could get a lot more attention.

Definitely one I’m keeping an eye on.

DYOR.
